key_insight: Applying neural network attention to segmented intracranial pressure (ICP) cardiac cycles reveals which waveform regions drive classification of patient body position, enabling data-driven discovery of physiologically meaningful features.
problem_solved: Lack of interpretable, automated methods to identify salient features in continuous ICP waveforms and link waveform morphology to patient state (here, body position) from clinical monitoring data.
method: Collect ICP waveforms from 60 patients and segment signals into individual cardiac cycles.
Train a convolutional neural network to classify each cycle into one of seven body positions.
Extract model attention maps to localize regions of the waveform that contribute most to the classification, producing interpretable regions of interest for feature discovery.
impact: Provides a practical, interpretable pipeline for extracting clinically relevant features from physiological time series using attention — useful for clinicians and ML practitioners building trustworthy, explainable models on biomedical waveform data.
visual_elements: Annotated ICP waveform with overlaid attention heatmap highlighting regions of interest across a cardiac cycle
Schematic of the pipeline: raw ICP → cardiac-cycle segmentation → CNN classifier → attention extraction → feature localization
Confusion matrix or bar chart of classification performance across the seven body positions
Illustration showing body-position labels (icons) matched to representative attended waveform shapes
paper_title: A Framework for Feature Discovery in Intracranial Pressure Monitoring Data Using Neural Network Attention
paper_authors: Jonathan D. Socha, Seyed F. Maroufi, Dipankar Biswas, Richard Um, Aruna S. Rao
